blocks.text: Insurance policies are dense legal contracts. You often deal with conflicting provisions where a grant of coverage in one section seems to be negated by an exclusion in another. Adjusters frequently lack the legal training to parse these interactions quickly. When you rush to meet file closure targets, the risk of misinterpreting a critical clause rises significantly. This creates a cycle where you feel pressured to move fast but are forced to slow down to avoid costly errors.
The financial cost of interpretation errors

The cost of a mistake in policy interpretation is not just about the claim payment. It includes the time spent on re-work, the potential for bad faith litigation, and the damage to carrier reputation. When you miss a subrogation opportunity because you misread a policy exclusion, you lose money that could have been recovered. This leakage adds up across a portfolio of claims and puts extra pressure on your daily performance metrics.

You can improve your accuracy by adopting a standard process for every file. First, extract the key facts of the loss before you even open the policy document. Second, use a digital search tool to find every instance of the relevant coverage terms. Do not rely on your memory for complex exclusions. Third, document your reasoning in a clear, linear format that explains why you applied a specific clause. This creates a trail that is easy for a supervisor or auditor to follow later.
How to use your Mac to speed up reviews

faq.question: How do I handle conflicting coverage language?
faq.answer: Always cross-reference the specific grant of coverage with the list of exclusions and endorsements. Document the conflict in your file notes and consult your supervisor if the intent remains unclear.

faq.question: Does Lazur change my policy language?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a tool to help you navigate and understand text. It does not edit your files or make coverage decisions for you.
